reason: The muscle-development signals are shown acting on developing cells and activating muscle genes, matching the first goal.
expectation: The cells should develop toward making muscle proteins.

alternatives.reason: The other signals suggest a separate route toward supporting cells.

effect: The signals produced young muscle cells that have active muscle genes but not yet the fibre bundles, so they may still need building blocks.
reaction: The picture makes the unfinished muscle cells clear.
reason: Amino acids are protein building blocks, and the young muscle cells have messages for muscle proteins.
expectation: The cells should use the building blocks to make muscle proteins.

alternatives.reason: I could start the separate supporting-cell goal first.

effect: The building blocks helped the young muscle cells make protein bundles, completing the muscle-cell goal. The supporting-cell goal remains.
reaction: The picture makes their progress toward muscle clear.
reason: The supporting-cell signals are shown acting on another group of developing cells, matching the remaining goal.
expectation: The signals should guide some cells toward becoming supporting cells.

effect: The signals produced young supporting cells with active support-protein genes, but they do not yet have a surrounding fibre network.
reaction: This parallels the muscle-cell development I just saw.
reason: Amino acids are protein building blocks, and these cells have messages for support proteins.
expectation: The cells should make supporting protein fibres from the building blocks.

effect: The supporting cells made fibres around themselves, completing the remaining goal. The result shows that cells with the same DNA and building blocks can make proteins for different jobs.
reaction: The contrast between proteins inside muscle cells and fibres around supporting cells was interesting.

mostWorthwhile.text: Making the supporting tissue was most worthwhile because it showed where the protein fibres end up and contrasted that with the muscle cells' bundles.

leastWorthwhile.text: The two signal-to-cell steps felt a little repetitive, although the parallel helped show that the same starting cells can develop in different directions.

surprise.text: I was surprised that the supporting cells released protein to make fibres around themselves, while the developing muscle cells kept their bundles inside.

arbitrary.text: None of the actions felt clearly arbitrary: the signals matched the cell types, and amino acids were presented as protein building blocks. The signals' detailed workings were not explained.

continue.text: I would try another chapter to see how these different cells and their proteins become parts of organs, though this chapter's repeated pairings were fairly predictable.
